mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which increases corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in less than 55% of instances despite rising GDPC1, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to higher wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in less than 50% of instances despite declining UNRATE, or the Rank IC is below 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 4.0% in a 3-month window, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in less than 40% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS>4.0% in 3 months), or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in residential investment (RSAFS) below 330,000 million dollars indicates a weakening housing market, which reduces consumer confidence and corporate capital expenditure, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 35% of triggered instances (RSAFS<330000), or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a weakening economy with both supply constraints and labor market deterioration, which triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (INDPRO decline and UNRATE rise) fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.01 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with a declining real GDP (GDPC1) signals a monetary tightening during an economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (FEDFUNDS rise and GDPC1 decline) fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market recovery (HOUST > 2000), a rising CPIAUCSL (indicating strong consumer demand) increases corporate revenue expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in less than 45% of triggered instances (HOUST>2000 and CPIAUCSL rising), or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market (UNRATE < 4.5%), a rising payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strong job growth, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in less than 40% of triggered instances (UNRATE<4.5% and PAYEMS rising), or the Rank IC is below 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.
